after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=-3+4\text{i}.$ 

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$
after.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13929099/recovery/assets/373ea8254a9816f67bfbcaf993348f409c1047284d09c43e5d41e68b15c5af58.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & ≈0.927\,30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)≈\pi -0.927\,30≈2.21
$$

to two decimal places.

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the positive real axis, then

\theta =arg⁡(z)=2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{11\pi }{6}.
$$
